explanation: Four papers intervene directly on model internals: pruning unsafe subnetworks (505), real-time unlearning (1223), activation steering (1315), and mechanistic bias localization (3096). All assume the intervention worked, yet the neighborhood contains no tool for independently auditing whether an edit actually removed the behavior, preserved capabilities, and didn't create new failures. The missing piece is a standardized 'edit verification' layer — a diff-and-regression harness for model surgery, analogous to CI tests for code. Given four intervention methods and zero verification methods, the gap is structural, not accidental.
verdict_reason: Edit verification is an established sub-field: MUSE, TOFU and RWKU test whether an intervention removed the behaviour while preserving capabilities, and capability regression is routinely measured with lm-evaluation-harness.
